findings.finding: all clock APIs are replaced by default

newMethod: installFixedDate(page): a Proxy replaces Date only; native timers, requestAnimationFrame, performance and Performance Timeline remain untouched.

oldEvidenceInterpretation.hostMs: Node process performance.now measurements are unaffected by page.clock and remain valid observations of host elapsed time for the OLD shimmed browser workload. They are not evidence of a native-clock workload and should not be directly mixed with new samples. The page load field hostReadyMs has the same limitation.
oldEvidenceInterpretation.browserMs: The old browserMs and browserReadyMs were elapsed synthetic clock ticks derived from Math.ceil(native performance.now), not native Performance API measurements. Keep as historical diagnostic data; do not use them as the corrected native-clock performance baseline.
oldEvidenceInterpretation.navigationAndPaint: Old empty arrays came from fakePerformance.getEntriesByType returning []; they do not establish missing or zero navigation/paint events.
oldEvidenceInterpretation.oldMethodologyCorrection: The old claim that performance.now, navigation timing and animation frames remain real was incorrect. This audit supersedes that claim without modifying or deleting the original records.
oldEvidenceInterpretation.screenshotsAndBehavior: Original screenshots and visible interaction observations remain historical evidence. A full default-entry run with native timers must compare existing PNGs without updating them to establish that the corrected clock preserves these baselines.

requiredGuardAssertions: Each page load has exactly one native Navigation Timing entry.
Each page load includes first-contentful-paint in native Paint Timing.
Date.now(), new Date().toISOString(), and Date() all resolve to the fixed wall time.
retention: Preserve earlier independent performance.json and full-run reports in their existing paths as records of the old method. Identify the corrected full-run performance attachment separately.
